title: Ravin (Rabbi Avin) son of Rav Nachman
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He was a distinguished student of Rav Yehudah, as in Bava Metzia 107a: “Rav Yehudah taught Ravin” (Rabbi Avin bar Rav Nachman, Dikdukei Soferim); and further there, Rav Yehudah said to him “Ravin my brother” several times. We likewise find in Yevamot 109b that he raised a difficulty against Rav Sheshet. In Menachot 26b, according to Dikdukei Soferim, Rav Chisda said to Ravin son of Rav Nachman, “I will explain it to you” — in the text Hyman used, Rav Yehudah addresses Rabbah bar Y. In Yevamot 84b he raises an objection and Rava resolves his words. He is mentioned in Bava Batra 94b: “Ravin son of Rav Nachman recited [a baraita].”

notes.text: ר״נ is read as Rav Nachman from the heading; רבא ב״י remains literal as Rava bar Y. Saved Davidson Menachot 26b has a different Ravin-bar-Rav-Ada/Rava exchange, and the supplemental 26a bounded check did not establish either quoted transmission. The supplied locator and both Hyman readings remain, with this unresolved source question held. תני denotes reciting a baraita here.

The earlier note records the state of the search before the exact passage was located. Hyman’s printed entry (vol. I, pp. 95–96) cites Bava Metzia 107a, where Rav Yehudah teaches Ravin and later addresses him three times as “Ravin my brother.” The supplied Hebrew cites Bava Batra. In Dikdukei Soferim on Menachot 26b (p. 60, note ת), the manuscript reading has Rav Chisda addressing Ravin bar Rav Nachman. The print column has Yehudah addressing Rabbah bar Rav Yitzchak, as does the consulted Menachot text. Hyman’s printed entry gives Rabbah bar Y., where the supplied Hebrew has Rava bar Y. The Ravin bar Rav Adda and Rava exchange cited in the earlier note is a separate exchange immediately afterward. In Yevamot 109b, Ravin responds to Rav Sheshet’s objection.
